title: Viking 1 & 2
tagline: Two explorers, four machines, one question: could Mars support life?
mystery: Two explorers. Four machines. One question: could Mars support life?
img.first.alt: The first photograph from the surface of Mars: rocks, dust and one of Viking 1's footpads
img.first.credit: First image from the surface of Mars, Viking 1, 20 July 1976. NASA/JPL
p1.where: 1975. Cape Canaveral, Florida. A Titan IIIE-Centaur rocket waits on Launch Complex 41.
p1.hello: We are Viking 1 and Viking 2. Each of us is two machines: an orbiter and a lander.
p1.question: Our big question: could Mars support life?
p1.went1: 20 August 1975. Viking 1 is on its way to Mars.
p1.swap: Viking-A was meant to go first, but its batteries had a problem. It flew second, as Viking 2.
p2.together: Each orbiter carried its lander, sealed inside a protective shell.
p2.course: Space is huge. Small engine burns keep us on course to Mars.
p2.hint: Slide to fire the thrusters. Stay in the green lane.
p2.win: On course! Viking 1 fired its engine on 27 Aug 1975, then 10 and 15 June 1976.
p2.arrive: Viking 1 reached Mars orbit on 19 June 1976. Viking 2 arrived on 7 August.
p3.eyes: Our orbiters stayed in space. They were our eyes above Mars.
p3.check: Before landing, we photographed the landing site. Was the ground safe?
p3.hint: Tap a site, then hold to take pictures with the orbiter's cameras.
p3.rough: Too rough! The first site in the Chryse region is not safe.
p3.safe: Smoother ground on the western slopes of Chryse Planitia.
p3.win: New target chosen! Viking 1 landed about 28 km from where it was aimed.
p4.separate: 20 July 1976. Viking 1's lander leaves its orbiter and falls towards Mars.
p4.air: On the way down, it even tasted the air.
p4.hint: Open the parachute at 6 km. Then drop the heat shield. Then fire the engines.
p4.win: Three legs on the Plains of Gold. The landing is perfect!
game.descent.early: Too early! NASA opened the parachute at 6 km.
game.descent.late: Too late! The parachute opens at 6 km.
game.descent.wait60: Wait until the parachute slows you to 60 m/s.
game.descent.noEngines: BUMP! Fire the landing engines before the ground.
p5.date: Viking 1 is down: the first truly successful landing on Mars.
p5.hint: Press SEND, then wait for the signal to cross space.
p5.heard: Earth heard us! Mission control cheered.
game.signal.patience: Patience! The signal is still flying.
game.signal.flying: Signal flying: {min} of {total} minutes (squeezed into {sec} seconds)
p5.apollo: The signal took 19 minutes. It was 7 years to the day after Apollo 11 landed on the Moon.
p5.first: The first photo ever taken on Mars: my own footpad, 25 seconds after landing.
p6.legs: I have no wheels. I stand on three legs, with two RTGs for power.
p6.lab: I am a laboratory: NASA's first search for life on another planet.
p6.hint: Tap an instrument, then hold until the bar is full.
p6.s.soil: 28 July 1976: my arm scooped up the first soil from Mars.
p6.s.bio: Three tests for life: Labeled Release, Gas Exchange, Pyrolytic Release.
p6.s.gcms: Iron-rich clay that gives off oxygen when wet. No organic molecules found.
p6.s.weather: My weather boom measures temperature, wind direction and wind speed.
p6.result: Strange chemistry, but no clear evidence of life. The question stayed open.
p7.land: 3 September 1976. Viking 2 lands at Utopia Planitia, about 6,460 km away.
p7.tilt: My twin's home is rockier and flatter. It came to rest tilted 8.5 degrees.
p8.photos: Our orbiters photographed Mars from above. Our landers photographed it from the ground.
p8.hint: Tap fast. Can the orbiters beat the landers' photos?
p8.valles: Viking 1's orbiter saw Valles Marineris, a canyon over 3,000 km long.
p8.apart: Our two landers rest about 6,460 km apart, on opposite sides of Mars.
p9.longer: The main mission ended in November 1976. We kept working for years.
p9.goal: Follow Viking to the last signal
p9.hint: Drag the timeline. Watch each machine fall silent.
p9.quiet: One by one, our signals went quiet.
tl.note: NASA pages differ by a day or two on some endings: shutdown, last data, or end of mission.
tl.primary: The primary mission ends. The work goes on.
tl.end.v2l: Viking 2's lander sends its last data.
tl.end.v1o: Viking 1's orbiter runs out of propellant on orbit 1,489.
tl.end.v1l: A faulty command interrupts Viking 1's lander. It never speaks again.
p10.result: We did not find proof that Mars was alive. But we measured it up close, for years.
p10.record: 52,663 pictures from above. 4,500 from the ground. Our gift to Earth.
p10.names: Viking 1's lander is now the Thomas Mutch Memorial Station. Viking 2's is the Gerald Soffen Memorial Station.
p10.last: Their signals ended. Their contribution did not.
